svg.title: Erdős #269 at the primes 2, 3, 5. A horizontal axis of multipliers from 1 to 5, drawn logarithmically. Four rows of the kernel, labelled by their powers of 2 (1, 8, 2, 4), are strips hatched red where the entry divided by its one-row prediction is 1/5 and blue where it is 1; each switches at its marker (1, 8/5, 2, 4), so the red parts form a staircase. Four columns, labelled by their powers of 3 (81, 3, 9, 1), are vertical probes at their thresholds 125/81, 5/3, 25/9 and 5. Below, row 1 is kept as a blue band and each difference of neighbouring rows is a red bar of value -4/5 on the interval between their switches: (1, 8/5], (8/5, 2] and (2, 4]. Each bar holds exactly one probe, and the probe at 5 meets only the kept row, so the four rows are independent. A rug of actual column thresholds on the axis shows columns in every gap. Under it, 1/60 divided by 1/12 equals 1/5: the entry at cutoff 6 against the copied row's prediction.
